envelopes: vectors/sealed-envelope/vectors.json (by id; the jwe member, exact ASCII)

conventions.paths: relative to the relay base URL, which has no trailing slash

placeholders.{mbx}: 16 fresh random bytes, base64url without padding; new for every case
placeholders.{token}: 32 fresh random bytes, base64url without padding; new for every case
placeholders.{collectHash}: base64url without padding of SHA-256 over the 32 decoded bytes of {token}
placeholders.{otherToken}: 32 further fresh random bytes, base64url without padding
placeholders.{now+N}: inside a text body: the integer the relay's clock reads plus N seconds, written as decimal digits

jsonValues.{\"$now\": N}: the integer the relay's clock reads plus N seconds

bodies.json: the object serialized as JSON without whitespace, after substitution
bodies.text: the exact characters, after placeholder substitution, as UTF-8
bodies.envelope: the jwe member of the named sealed-envelope vector
bodies.padEnvelope: the named vector's jwe with its fourth segment extended by repeating A until the whole text has the given length
bodies.fill: the given character repeated to the given length

conventions.requestHeaderValues: a string is one field line; an array is that many field lines with the same name, in order
conventions.requestHeaders: Content-Length is sent with the body's length unless omitContentLength is true, in which case the body is sent with the chunked transfer coding (HTTP/1.1) or without Content-Length (HTTP/2)
conventions.clockHook: how a harness sets a relay's clock is up to the implementation under test; the reference harness POSTs {"now": <integer seconds>} to a test-only URL. A controlled case starts with the clock set to 1792000000, which may move the clock backward between cases; every case uses fresh ids, so this is harmless
conventions.advance: a step that moves the relay's clock forward by the given seconds; only in cases whose clock is controlled
conventions.clock: absent: the case runs against any relay and needs no clock control, and {now+N} and $now use the harness's own clock, assumed within a few seconds of the relay's; controlled: the harness must set and advance the relay's clock, and starts it at an integer second

expect.problemType: the problem details type member (RFC 9457); the body is application/problem+json and its status member equals the status
expect.headers: each named response header must be present. Matchers: "delta-seconds", a value of one or more digits; "present", any value; {mediaType}, type and subtype equal ignoring case and parameters; {methods}, the comma-separated list holds exactly these methods in any order; {bearerChallenge: "no-error"}, a Bearer challenge (scheme name in any case) with no error parameter; {bearerChallenge: "invalid_token"}, a Bearer challenge whose error parameter is invalid_token. Other parameters, such as realm, are allowed. A plain string must match exactly
expect.bodyEquals: the response body is byte-identical to the named body
